findings.text: You need an ngrok account and an auth token to tunnel your local development environment.
findings.quote: ACE creates tunnels using the ngrok Node.js module, which can be used free of charge after creating an ngrok account. In order to use ngrok in ACE, an auth token is all that's required.

findings.text: Create an ngrok account and obtain an authtoken.
findings.quote:
Create a new ngrok account

Obtain an authtoken

Copy your personal token value (you'll need this later)

findings.text: Sign up for a cloud development site.
findings.quote:
Go to go.atlassian.com/cloud-dev and sign up. It may take
several minutes to provision your site.

findings.text: Enable development mode in your Atlassian cloud site.
findings.quote:
Under User-installed apps, click Settings.

Select Enable development mode, and then click Apply.

findings.text: Create an app descriptor file named atlassian-connect.json.
findings.quote: In the project directory, create a new file named atlassian-connect.json with this content:

findings.text: Create a static HTML file for the app user interface.
findings.quote: In your project directory, create a new file named helloworld.html with this content:

findings.text: Host the app files on a local web server.
findings.quote:
Start the server on port 8000 by running:

1
2

http-server -p 8000

findings.text: Expose the local web server to the internet using ngrok.
findings.quote:
In a new command line window, run this command to expose your web server to the internet. If your app is not
running on port 8000, change the command to use your app's port number.

1
2

ngrok http 8000

findings.text: Update the app descriptor with the ngrok HTTPS URL.
findings.quote: Edit the app descriptor file, and set the baseUrl property to the ngrok HTTPS URL.

findings.text: Install the app in the Atlassian cloud instance using the descriptor URL.
findings.quote:
Navigate to Jira in your Atlassian Cloud instance, then choose Jira settings (cog icon) > Apps > Manage apps.

Click Upload app.

In the From this URL field, provide a link to your app descriptor.

findings.text: The app descriptor file can only be fetched from specific web server ports.
findings.quote: The descriptor file can only be fetched from web server ports 80, 443, or 8080.

findings.text: New Connect apps cannot be published to the Atlassian Marketplace.
findings.quote:
You can no longer publish Connect apps on the Atlassian Marketplace. All new extensibility features
will be delivered only on Forge.

findings.text: Bundle CSS and JS files with your site for production environments.
findings.quote: For production environments, we recommend bundling CSS and JS files with your site, rather than relying on a third-party CDN.

findings.text: The default global hourly quota for apps is 65,000 points.
findings.quote: Tier 1 – Global Pool (default) Your app shares a single 65,000 point hourly quota across all tenants. This is the default tier for all apps.

findings.text: Per-tenant rate limits are capped at 500,000 points per hour.
findings.quote: Per-tenant rate limits are capped at 500,000 points per hour for Standard, Premium, and Enterprise editions.

findings.text: The short window limit for per-issue write operations is 20 operations per 2 seconds.
findings.quote: Short window: 20 write operations per 2 seconds

findings.text: The long window limit for per-issue write operations is 100 operations per 30 seconds.
findings.quote: Long window: 100 write operations per 30 seconds

findings.text: The default burst limit for GET requests is 100 requests per second.
findings.quote: HTTP method Requests per second GET 100

findings.text: The default burst limit for POST requests is 100 requests per second.
findings.quote: HTTP method Requests per second POST 100

findings.text: The default burst limit for PUT requests is 50 requests per second.
findings.quote: HTTP method Requests per second PUT 50

findings.text: The default burst limit for DELETE requests is 50 requests per second.
findings.quote: HTTP method Requests per second DELETE 50

findings.text: Forge is the preferred cloud app development platform for Atlassian.
findings.quote: Forge is the preferred cloud app development platform for Atlassian, and we’re adding new capabilities every week.

findings.text: Developers can obtain a free cloud developer site for testing purposes.
findings.quote: Get a cloud developer site to test your app. It's free forever.

findings.text: You must create an OAuth 2.0 integration in the developer console to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
findings.quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.

findings.text: You can choose between account-level or resource-level grant types when creating an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
findings.quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, you can choose between two grant types: Account-level grant: The user’s consent applies at the Atlassian account level. A single grant can cover access to multiple sites where your app is installed, subject to the scopes you request. Resource-level grant: The user’s consent is limited to the specific site(s) they select on the consent screen.

findings.text: Navigate to the developer console to create an app.
findings.quote: From any page on developer.atlassian.com, select your profile icon in the top-right corner, and from the dropdown, select Developer console.

findings.text: Select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration.
findings.quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.

findings.text: Enter an app name and choose the grant type.
findings.quote: Enter an app name and choose the OAuth 2.0 (3LO) grant type for your app.

findings.text: Configure OAuth 2.0 (3LO) in the Authorization menu.
findings.quote: Select Authorization in the left menu. Next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO), select Configure.

findings.text: Enter the Callback URL and save changes.
findings.quote: Enter the Callback URL. Set this to any URL that is accessible by the app. When you implement OAuth 2.0 (3LO) in your app (see next section), the redirect_uri must match this URL. Click Save changes.

findings.text: Add APIs to the app via the Permissions menu.
findings.quote: Select Permissions in the left menu. Next to the API you want to add, select Add.

findings.text: You cannot delete an app if it is currently installed on a site.
findings.quote: You can only delete an app if it's not installed anywhere. If your app is currently installed on a site, uninstall it.

findings.text: Atlassian recommends clearly identifying your app in the Marketplace.
findings.quote: Clearly identify your app in the Marketplace (recommended).

findings.text: The implicit grant flow is not supported.
findings.quote: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) currently supports the code grant flow only. It does not support the implicit grant flow.

findings.text: The App Key cannot be changed after it is set.
findings.quote: App Key - the unique identifier for the Marketplace app. This value can't be altered once you set it.

findings.text: A build number is mandatory for the Marketplace app.
findings.quote: Build number - the unique identifier for each build, which determines the order of different versions of the Marketplace app. This field is mandatory.

findings.text: Select the option that your app is not directly installable on the publish page.
findings.quote: On the Publish a new app page, select My app isn't directly installable to see the following options:

findings.text: You must provide access to a test instance of your software for the review team.
findings.quote: In order to test the integration we will need access to a test instance of your software so we can run through the set up and configuration.

findings.text: Complete the final pre-submission checklist.
findings.quote: 1. Complete the final pre-submission checklist

findings.text: Submit your app for review via the partner portal.
findings.quote: Submit your app for review via the partner portal

findings.text: Respond to review feedback from the review team.
findings.quote: 3. Respond to review feedback

findings.text: Verify the listing is live and test the installation.
findings.quote: 4. Post-approval verification

findings.text: Incomplete listing fields, missing policy links, or install failures on a clean site cause review rejections.
findings.quote: Most review rejections come from avoidable gaps like incomplete listing fields, missing policy links, or install failures on a clean site.

findings.text: All new publicly listed apps must be approved by Atlassian.
findings.quote: All new publicly listed apps need to be approved by Atlassian.

findings.text: Partners must have a privacy and security tab and ticket approval.
findings.quote: Privacy and security tab and ticket approval

findings.text: Partners must have a partner verification ticket.
findings.quote: Partner verification ticket

findings.text: Partners must accept the Marketplace Partner Agreement upon submission.
findings.quote: Upon submission, accept the Marketplace Partner Agreement.

findings.text: Partners must create a privacy policy.
findings.quote: Create a privacy policy

findings.text: At least one contact from the partner profile must be registered with the Atlassian Developer Community.
findings.quote: At least one contact from your partner profile is registered with the Atlassian Developer Community for future correspondence.

findings.text: Approval for apps takes 10-15 business days.
findings.quote: Approvals take 10-15 business days, but approval times vary depending on current volume and the Marketplace team’s availability.

findings.text: Apps that break the host Atlassian app UI will be rejected.
findings.quote: If the UI breaks, your app will be rejected.

findings.text: Trademark infringement results in automatic rejection.
findings.quote: Trademark infringement is an automatic rejection, so be sure to read our brand guidelines for Marketplace Partners before submitting your app.

findings.text: Basic authentication is not permitted for public, approved apps.
findings.quote: Whilst your app may make use of Basic authentication with Atlassian's product REST APIs for ease of development/speed during development, this shall not be the case for any public, approved app.

findings.text: Do not use prohibited words in your app name.
findings.quote: Prohibited words: Do not use "Atlassian," "plugin," "beta," "add-on," or "app."

findings.text: Do not start your app name with an Atlassian product name.
findings.quote: Branding: Do not start with an Atlassian product name. Use "Time Tracker for Jira," not "Jira Time Tracker."

findings.text: The app name must be 60 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: App name (max 60 characters): Use a unique, distinctive name.

findings.text: The tagline must be 130 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Tagline (max 130 characters): A punchy, scannable phrase summarizing the app's purpose.

findings.text: The summary must be 250 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Summary (max 250 characters): Used in search results to provide deeper context than the tagline.

findings.text: Videos should be under 30 seconds.
findings.quote: Video (highly recommended): Keep it under 30 seconds. Show the app solving a real problem, not a marketing montage.

findings.text: Primary highlight screenshots must be 1840 by 900 pixels.
findings.quote: Use 1840×900 px (hi-res) for primary highlights.

findings.text: Screenshot captions must be 220 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Every screenshot must have a caption (max 220 characters) that explains the specific feature shown.

findings.text: Highlight titles must be 50 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Highlight title (max 50 characters): Name the specific outcome.

findings.text: Highlight summaries must be 220 characters or fewer.
findings.quote: Highlight summary (max 220 characters): Explain the benefit.

findings.text: Cropped screenshots must be 580 by 330 pixels.
findings.quote: Cropped screenshot (580×330 px): A focused view of the feature.

findings.text: You must create and verify your Atlassian organization.
findings.quote: Create/verify company Atlassian account and organization profile

findings.text: You must enroll as a Marketplace Partner.
findings.quote: Enroll as a Marketplace Partner on the Atlassian Marketplace

findings.text: You must accept the Marketplace Partner Agreement and Terms of Use.
findings.quote: Accept Marketplace Partner Agreement and Terms of Use

findings.text: You must complete the partner due diligence process.
findings.quote: Complete partner due diligence process

findings.text: You must enable 2-step verification for security partners.
findings.quote: Enable 2-step verification for security partners

findings.text: Marketplace Partner enrollment is a prerequisite for listing any app.
findings.quote: Enrollment is a prerequisite for listing any app.

findings.text: Create or verify your company Atlassian account and organization profile.
findings.quote: Create/verify company Atlassian account and organization profile

findings.text: Enroll as a Marketplace Partner on the Atlassian Marketplace.
findings.quote: Enroll as a Marketplace Partner on the Atlassian Marketplace

findings.text: Assign roles for your team members.
findings.quote: Assign roles for Primary, Support, Licensing/Finance, Security, Marketing, Engineering, and Sales Support

findings.text: Connect is a development framework for extending Atlassian cloud products.
findings.quote: Connect is a development framework for extending Atlassian cloud products. Connect gives you control over the tech stack, infrastructure, and integration with Atlassian Cloud products.

findings.text: You can create a basic app by defining an app descriptor file and a static HTML page.
findings.quote: An app consisting of an app descriptor and an HTML page is the most basic Atlassian Connect app.

findings.text: Atlassian recommends bundling CSS and JS files with your site for production environments.
findings.quote: For production environments, we recommend bundling CSS and JS files with your site, rather than relying on a third-party CDN.

findings.text: Atlassian recommends using a hosting site like Bitbucket for open-source apps.
findings.quote: We recommend a hosting site like Bitbucket. Include a license file in your source code that matches what you report in the Marketplace.

findings.text: Atlassian recommends placing reminders for upgrades or complementary products in configuration screens.
findings.quote: We recommend placing these reminders in configuration screens.

findings.text: Atlassian recommends listing apps as paid-via-vendor if they require a third-party account.
findings.quote: We recommend in most cases these apps be listed as paid-via-vendor, unless your app provides some useful functionality without the third-party account.

findings.text: The approval process for apps takes 10-15 business days.
findings.quote: Approvals take 10-15 business days, but approval times vary depending on current volume and the Marketplace team’s availability.

findings.text: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.
findings.quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.

findings.text: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.
findings.quote: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing.

findings.text: Although OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps can be listed on the Atlassian Marketplace, they will appear as informational listings only, with limited Marketplace features.
findings.quote: Although OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps can be listed on the Atlassian Marketplace, they will appear as informational listings only, with limited Marketplace features.
